chunks: From him, from Yusuf ibn Aqil, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him)
That he ruled regarding a will that was witnessed only by a woman, so he validated one-quarter of the will based on the testimony of a woman.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: How is a will validated if it is witnessed only by a woman according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) narrates from Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) regarding a legal ruling on wills (wasiyyah). When a will is witnessed solely by a woman, the Imam ruled that it is validated for one-quarter of its total value, applying the standard ratio of a woman's testimony being half that of a man's in financial matters. This ruling highlights the practical application of Quranic testimony ratios in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between the validity of the document's execution and the extent of its enforceable value.
